case_summary.text: GST : Where applicant has been awarded a contract by Airport Authority of India for construction of residential colony for staff and employees, construction of residential colony by applicant attracts GST at rate of 12 per cent as per entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017
12% GST on construction of residential colony for staff and employees of Airport Authority of India : AAR
18% GST to be levied on services of construction of staff quarters provided to a government entity : AAR

GST : Works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for Airport Authorities of India performed by applicant being used in process of commerce and business is appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent
12% GST on construction of residential quarters exclusively meant for use of employees of NPCIL up to 31.12.2021: AAAR
GST : Supply of service of construction of staff quarters to be provided to a government entity is not entitled to concessional rate of 12% GST; such service attracts 18% GST
GST : Supply of service of construction of staff quarters to be provided to a government entity is not entitled to concessional rate of 12% GST; Such service attracts 18% GST.

GST : Where execution of works contract service for construction of residential quarters by applicant-civil contractor is exclusively meant for use of employees of government entity NPCIL, and aforesaid construction is ancillary to attainment of main object of NPCIL, applicant is eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST for period up to 31-12-2021

GST : Where applicant enters into contract with a company for construction of residential complex, its case would be covered under concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since project undertaken by them falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing'. However,

GST : Where applicant who is promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing residential housing project 'Akriti', works contract service received from contractors for construction of those dwelling units that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of said notification, provided applicant does not opt for paying tax at rate specified in Entry No. 3(ie) Entry No. 3(if)
Construction of new civil structures for Airport Authority of India chargeable at 18% GST

GST : Construction of semi-finished affordable housing and other residential apartment will be subject to GST at rate of 1 percent and 5 percent respectively as contract entered for providing such service is inseparable from contract entered for sale of such structure

GST : Where applicant is engaged in business of construction and development of residential and commercial complex, since project undertaken by it falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing', applicant's case is covered under tax rate of 12 per cent under Heading No. 9954 (Construction Services), mentioned in Notification No. 11/2017-CT-(Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : If projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, construction service provided by applicant to developer under residential project is liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent KGST as provided in Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; else, services will be liable to tax at rate of 9 per cent under CGST Act and at rate of 9 per cent under KGST Act as provided in Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : If projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, construction service provided by applicant to developer under residential project is liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent KGST as provided in Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; else,

GST : Where construction of residential quarters for employees of power plant are exclusively meant for use of employees of NPCIL, a government entity, and aforesaid construction is ancillary to attainment of main object of NPCIL, therefore applicant-assessee is eligible for concessional rate of 12% under Entry 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T.(Rate) dated 28.06.2017 for period up to 31.12.2021.

GST : Where applicant constructed residential units on land belonging to flood victims under a rehabilitation project awarded to it by a charitable trust, activity squarely falls within scope of works contract under section 2(119) and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017
Construction services provided for project covered under ‘Affordable Housing’ attract 12% GST w.e.f. 25-1-2018

GST: Where activity of construction of flats allotted by MPPGCL to applicant does not have any relation to principal work of power generation entrusted by State Government to MPPCGL, work contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST)

GST : Where applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), activity undertaken by applicant is supply of works contract service to a Govt. entity covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST
Construction services relating to affordable housing project provided after 25.01.2018 attract 12% GST

GST : Where applicant is engaged in development of residential project called 'SAMANVAY RESIDENCY', which falls under affordable housing project, construction services provided by applicant qualifies for reduced tax rate of 12 per cent GST as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017
18% GST leviable on construction of airport terminal buildings, high security prison etc. for PWD/Govt. entities: AAR

GST: Where State Government of Madhya Pradesh awarded a contract to applicant, a 100 per cent State Government hold company, to construct a Thermal Power Project and further applicant awarded a contract to one 'S' towards construction of certain residential quarters at Thermal Power Project, work contract awarded by applicant to 'S' for construction of residential quarters shall attract GST at rate of 18 per cent under Heading No. 9954

GST : Construction of airport terminal buildings, high security prison, residential school complex and development of green field airport for PWD / government entities are liable to GST of 18 per cent
GST : Construction services provided to State Housing Board with respect to construction of Police Station as a main contractor/sub-contractor are liable to 18 per cent GST

GST : Where contract was awarded to applicant by public works department of State Government for construction of Airport Terminal Building, allied buildings/facilities and associated works and development of airport, it is liable to 18 per cent GST
Sub-contract for construction of independent houses under ‘Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana’ attracts 12% GST

CGST : Where project 'Prajapati Magnum' undertaken by applicants falls under definition of "Affordable Housing", applicant's case is covered under tax rate of 12% under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v) (da) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, but benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018 i.e. date on which Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and benefit of this reduced rate would be

GST : Composite supply of works contract that includes construction of school building, school and college hostel, staff quarters, etc. provided to State Government is subject to 12% GST as it is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : Composite supply of works contract that includes construction of school building, school and college hostel, staff quarters, etc provided to State Government is subject to 12% GST as it is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : Where applicant has entered into a sub-contract agreement for execution of works contract pertaining to construction of independent houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana with main contractor, who has been awarded contract, sub-contract is covered under sub-item (c) of item (iv) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to CGST at 6 per cent + SGST at 6 per cent

GST: Construction service provided by applicant contractor under project 'La-Riveria', which is an affordable housing project, qualifies for application of lower rate of CGST of 6 per cent and SGST of 6 per cent w.e.f. 25-1-2018 as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended vide Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018

GST : GST on construction of unit which is other than affordable residential apartments by applicant in Residential Real Estate Project(RREP) promoted by them, namely, Ashiana Shubham-Phase IV in Chennai is classifiable under SAC 9954 as 'Construction Service' and applicable rate of tax is CGST at rate of 3.75 per cent and SGST at rate of 3.75 per cent as per Entry Sl. No. 3(ia) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended
Works contract for construction of residential quarters at Thermal Power Project attract 18% GST

GST : Where applicant sub-contracts for construction of independent houses under main contract of construction of houses pertaining to Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana is covered under sub-item (c) of item (iv) of serial number 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 is liable to CGST at 6 per cent and similarly same is also liable to KGST at 6 per cent under Karnataka Goods and Services Act, 2017

GST : Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for Karnataka Slum Development Board under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana as a main contractor is liable to 12% GST (6% CGST + 6% SGST) till 17-7-2022 in terms of Sl. No. 3(iv)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended and thereafter, such services are liable to 18% GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of said Notification. However, these services when provided by sub-contractor are also liable to 18% GST.
12% GST leviable on contract for construction of new building of railway station

GST : Since applicant-assessee is engaged in construction services and undertook work contract tendered by Rajasthan Housing Board on 25-1-2021 under scheme of Chief Minister Jan Awas Yojna 2015 programme, therefore, as per Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 services provided by assessee will attract a rate of 18 per cent GST

GST : Where applicant is engaged in promotion of gated community villas for prospective villa buyers and it buys land and divides same into plots and sells plots to villa buyers and while booking of plots happens it enters into construction agreement with villa buyers to construct and transfer villa to villa buyers on payment of agreed consideration as per agreed conditions in construction agreement, applicant is liable to pay GST at rate of 1.5 per cent in respect of services of construction of affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (i) and at rate of 7.5 per cent in respect of services of construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item (ia) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 subject to conditions prescribed under respective entries in villa projects

GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

GST : Where applicant, engaged in providing construction services, undertook work contract tendered by Rajasthan Housing Board under scheme of Chief Minister Jan Awas Yojna 2015, services provided by assessee will attract a rate of 18 per cent GST as per Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

GST : Where applicant developer provides flats on lease to prospective customers, there is a taxable supply of services in form of construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, to their prospective lessees transaction is a composite supply of works contract as defined in clause 119 of section 2 and classifiable under Heading No. 9954 (ii) and will attract tax at rate of 18 per cent
Construction & Development of project ‘Samanvay Residency’ covered under Affordable Housing in GST is taxable at 12%
12% GST to be levied on Construction Services for affordable housing projects having infrastructure status by Govt.

GST : Villas being constructed by applicant are "residential apartment", projects are "real estate project" and applicant is "promoter"; services of applicant are construction of residential apartments other than affordable residential apartments as per entry at Item No. (ia) of SI. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 ibid and liable to GST @ 7.5% deduction of one-third of total amount charged for supply in arriving at taxable value of supply,

GST : Where ongoing residential project did not fall under affordable housing scheme, services of construction of all types of residential apartments in said ongoing housing project during period from 1-7-2017 to 31-3-2019 do not qualify for concessional rate of 12 per cent and is liable to GST at rate of 18 per cent as per item (i) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Where applicant is awarded a contract with Railways for construction of new building of railway station, new constructions involved in contract are taxable at 12 per cent GST as per Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under 'residual item' under item No. (xii) of Serial No.3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6- 2017

GST : Activities of APIIC are essentially business oriented, and hence, construction services provided by applicant to APIIC are not eligible for concessional rate of 12% under Notification No.24/2017-CT (Rate) dated 21.09.2017; applicant's contract is classifiable under SAC heading No. 9954 under construction services and it is Composite Supply of Works Contract liable to 18% (9% CGST and 9% SGST)

Needless to mention that such supply shall not qualify for exemption as envisaged under Sr. No. 3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate), inasmuch as the said supply is a 'Pure Service' and not in the nature of works contract service. [Para 4.6] The works entrusted to the applicant namely construction of 800 seater boys hostel, 200 seater girls hostel, Construction of lecture hall complex, Construction of Student Activity Centre, Dispensary, Construction of 1000 capacity Auditorium, Construction of Central Research and Instrumentation facilities, Construction of Central Workshop, Play grounds are within the purview of sub-clause (b) of clause (vi) of Sl. No. 3 (heading 9954) of Notification No. 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate) under CGST Act and corresponding notification under OGST Act, 2017, and hence merit exemption where the applicable tax rate is 12 per cent (6 per cent under CGST & 6 per cent under OGST Act, 2017). [Para 4.7]

The works contract so executed by the applicant includes Sewerage disposal (Sewerage and STP) unit and construction of water works are covered vide Sl. No. (iii) (c) to the said notification and merit exemption where the applicable tax rate is 12 per cent (6 per cent under CGST & 6 per cent under OGST Act, 2017). [Pra 4.8]

Now coming to the issue of construction of Directors Bungalow and construction of staff-faculty quarters. It is seen that the applicant has been awarded construction of Directors Bungalow, 40 nos. staff quarters, 84 nos. Faculty Quarters in the IIT Campus, Bhubaneswar. It is also observed that the civil construction of residential quarters is not the primary work entrusted to IIT, Bhubaneswar. Accordingly, why the benefit of concessional rate at the rate of 12 per cent GST should be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant? The intention of the Legislature has been to allow concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of IIT, Bhubaneswar will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. Hence, construction of Directors Bungalow and construction of staff/faculty quarters is out of purview of exemption provided under Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST). [Para 4.9]

In view of the discussions foregoing, it is held that the works entrusted to the applicant by IIT, Bhubaneswar under contract/agreement dated 2-5-2016 cannot be termed as composite supply and, thus, entire work under the said contract shall not be entitled to concessional rate in terms of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. However, it is also held that the supply of goods and/or services or both which squarely fall within the ambit of scope of work entrusted to IIT, Bhubaneswar by Government of India shall be entitled for concessional rate under Sl. No. 3(vi) to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), 28-6-2017 (R). Accordingly, each and every supply under the subject contract shall be treated separately for determining the rate of tax under the CGST Act, 2017 read with the provisions of GST Tariff and respective exemption notifications. [Para 4.10]

The Authority is not inclined to subscribe to the contentions of the applicant. The fact still remains that the sole work entrusted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh to the applicant is of generation of electricity (power) in the State of Madhya Pradesh. Construction of residential quarters though within the precincts of power plant cannot by any stretch of argument and imagination be termed as the work entrusted to applicant. [Para 7.6] The applicant has further argued that Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 provides a concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent with the conditions mentioned in Column 5 of the table as under:

'Provided that where the services are supplied to a Government Entity, they should have been procured by the said entity in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or local authority, as the case may be.'

Now the applicant has tried to argue that it has been entrusted the work of construction of residential quarters also by the State Government. However, nothing has been placed before the Authority to substantiate such claim. In absence of any specific mention of construction of residential quarters having been entrusted to the applicant by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, there is no reason to deviate from the stand taken in the matter of application filed by Shreeji Infrastructure India (P.) Ltd.vide Order No. 15/2018, dated 18-10-2018. [Para 7.8]

In yet another question placed before the Authority the applicant has sought ruling on rate of GST applicable on construction contracts of residential quarters at various power stations of the applicant. However, it is a very generic question which cannot be decided without looking into specific contracts being awarded. The Authority thus refrains from giving any categorical ruling on the second question. [Para 7.9]

In view of the aforesaid, inasmuch as the tender document covered in the application is concerned, the GST will be applicable at the rate of 18 per cent under Heading No. 9954 inasmuch as it refers to construction of residential quarters, which was awarded to Shreeji Infrastructure (P.) Ltd. [Para 7.10]

Ruling

The work contract awarded to Shreeji Infrastructure (P.) Ltd. for construction of residential quarters at Thermal Power Project shall attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) under Heading No. 9954. [Para 8.1]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of civil structures - Heading No. 9954 (Construction Services) - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works Contract - Applicant has been awarded a project by Airport Authority of India (AAI) which is in nature of works contract - Scope of project is development and upgradation of Airports by construction or extension of Runway, construction of new Taxi track, Apron, Isolation bay, Perimeter road and other allied works - It has sought advance ruling in respect of applicable rate of tax on works allotted by AAI - It is found that applicant is undertaking a works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for AAI which are used in process of commerce and business - Entry at Serial number 3(vi)(a) specifically provides that works be 'meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession - Whether therefore, works contract performed by applicant cannot be considered as covered under Serial No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 6 per cent, but are more appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax, dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent - Held, yes [Paras 7 and 8]GST : Works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for Airport Authorities of India performed by applicant being used in process of commerce and business is appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent

FACT: The applicant is engaged in works contract relating to execution of large-scale infrastructure projects, like Airports, Defence Industrial/ Technical Buildings, Hospitals, Housing, Steel Structural, Highways, and Bridges. The applicant is undertaking a contract of works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for the Airport Authorities of India. The Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India has shown in the company profile that the shareholding of the Government of India in the Airport Authorities of India is 100 per cent and hence the AAI is a Government Entity.[Para 7.6] Further, the issue is whether the constructed works is a civil structure or any other original works. The runway and the apron etc. are structures which bear the load of the aircraft and provide a stable surface for the aircraft to operate. These are, therefore, civil structures. As per the AAI letters submitted by the applicant it is clear that the applicant is engaged in the extension of the runway and construction of new aprons and allied areas. Extension of the runway requires a new construction to be carried out and so does the apron and other areas. Therefore the applicant is engaged in construction of new civil structures. The term 'original works' is not defined in the Act, but the definition is provided in the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, to mean all new constructions;

(i)

all types of additions and alterations to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are required to make them workable;

(ii)

erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery or equipment or structures, whether pre-fabricated or otherwise.

The applicant is, therefore, engaged in construction of new civil structures. The activities carried out by the applicant are covered under the relevant serial number of the Notification. [Para 7.7]

The next issue is whether these works are meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession? In this regard, the original works done by the applicant are for use by the Airports Authority of India for supplying services to the Airway operations and hence is in the course of business. The airlines that use the runway and the aprons etc. constructed by the applicant work with a view to earn profits. They are engaged in commerce and business. Entry at Serial number 3(vi)(a) specifically provides that works be 'meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession'. As the works carried out by the applicant are used in the process of commerce and business, the applicant does not qualify for the works to be classified under Serial number 3(vi)(a). Hence the works contract performed by the applicant cannot be considered as covered under Serial No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 6 per cent, but are more appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of the of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent.[Para 7.8]

An explanation has been inserted to the above entry by Notification No. 17/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 26-7-2018, which provides that for the purposes of this item, the term 'business' shall not include any activity or transaction undertaken by the Central Government, a State Government or any local authority in which they are engaged as public authorities. Even with this insertion, the activities or transactions undertaken by the Central Government, State Government and a Local Authority, in which they are engaged as public authorities alone are to be excluded from the scope of 'business' for the purposes of this entry. This Explanation does not exclude a Government Entity and hence the situation remains unchanged even by the aforesaid insertion of explanation so far as the activity of the applicant is concerned. [Para 7.9]

Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in Column 3 of the Table in the said Notification, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein. One of the recommendations made by the GST Council in its 25th meeting held on 18-1-2018 at Delhi was to extend the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sq. m. in a housing project which has been given infrastructure status under Notification No. 13/06/2009, dated 30-3-2009. The said notification of Department of Economic Affairs provides infrastructure status to Affordable Housing. The recommendation of the Council would extend the concessional rate to construction of flats/houses of less than 60 sq. m. in projects other than the projects covered by any scheme of the Central or State Government also. The GST Council has also observed that it may be recalled that all inputs used in and capital goods deployed for construction of flats, houses, etc. attract GST of 18 per cent or 28 per cent. As against this, most of the housing projects in the affordable segment in the country would now attract GST of 8 per cent (after deducting value of land). As a result, the builder or developer will not be required to pay GST on the construction service of flats etc. in cash but would have enough ITC (input tax credits) in his books to pay the output GST, in which case, he should not recover any GST payable on the flats from the buyers. He can recover GST from the buyers of flats only if he recalibrates the cost of flat after factoring in the full ITC available in the GST regime and reduces the ex-GST price of flats. The GST Council has also mentioned that the builders/developers are expected to follow the principles laid down under section 171 of the GST Act (Anti-Profiteering Rules) scrupulously.

Whether the housing project qualifies as affordable housing project or not, shall be determined by the builder/developer as per the definition of affordable housing given in the abovementioned notification (i.e., affordable housing has been defined as a housing project using at least 50 per cent of FAR/FSI for dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 SQM). However, the civil construction of residential quarters is neither the primary work entrusted to MPPGCL nor it has any bearing on the work i.e. power generation by any means. Thus, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent GST should not be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant. The intention of the legislature has been to give concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general. Any work having direct involvement in the entrusted work i.e. power generation would merit exemption envisaged under Sr.No.3(vi)(c) of the Notification No.11/2017-CT (Rate) under CGST Act and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of MPPGCL will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. [Para 5.5]

The activity in question definitely did not have any relation to the principal work of power generation entrusted by the State Government to MPPGCL, and, thus, the works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No.11/2017-CT Rate dated 28-6-2017 and corresponding notification under MPGST Act, 2017. [Para 5.6]

Thus, the impugned activity of the applicant would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) classifiable under SAC 9954 read with Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017. [Para 5.7]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Civil construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant-company is engaged in business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor - It seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether construction services proposed to be provided by applicant will qualify for reduced GST rate of 12 per cent as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Low cost houses in an affordable housing project having area of 60 sq. mts. or upto 60 sq. mts. will attract 12 per cent GST - Whether since project undertaken by applicant is an affordable housing project, it will attract rate of 12 per cent GST under Sr. No. 3 of said Notification – Held, yes [Para 5.8][In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant undertook project of construction of residential flat (Low cost flats) having carpet area of upto or less than 60 sq. mts. and its project falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing Project', applicant's case is covered under concessional tax rate slab of 12 per cent

FACT: The applicant-company is engaged in the business of civil construction of residential premises as a contractor. It had filed the instant application in respect of a proposed civil construction contract to be entered into with a developer for construction of a residential project comprising of 135 buildings all having residential flats/units having carpet area of up to or less than 60 Sq. Mts. According to them, since more than 50 per cent of PSI is utilized towards construction of LCH, the project would qualify as an 'Affordable Housing Project' (AHP).

It seeks advance ruling on the issue as to whether the construction services proposed to be provided by the applicant will qualify for the reduced CGST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST), as provided in Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

HELD: As per Sr. No. 3, item (v)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) dated 25-1-2018, low-cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house in an affordable housing project which has been given infrastructure status vide notification of Government of India, in Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs vide F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated the 30-3-2017 will attract tax rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST.) [Para 5.3]

This clause will be applicable to the applicant if the project undertaken by them is an affordable housing project which has been given infrastructure status vide Government of India notification mentioned above. [Para 5.4]

Department of Economic Affairs' notification issued vide F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated the 30th March,2017 has included Affordable Housing under the column 'Infrastructure sub-sector' against the category of Social and Commercial Infrastructure. [Para 5.5]

One of the recommendations made by the GST Council in its 25th meeting held on 18-1-2018 at Delhi was to extend the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sq. mts. in a housing project which has been given infrastructure status under Notification No.13/06/2009 dated 30-3-2009. The said notification of Department of Economic Affairs provides infrastructure status to Affordable Housing. The recommendation of the Council would extend the concessional rate to construction of flats/houses of less than 60 sq. mts. in projects other than the projects covered by any scheme of the Central or State Government also. [Para 5.6]

Mts.), applicant’s case is covered under Heading No. 9954 eligible for concessional tax rate of 12 per cent; in case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. or which are commercial units, applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate

FACT: The applicant has entered into civil construction contract with 'J' Ltd. in respect of seven residential buildings.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on question as to whether the construction services proposed to be provided by the applicant under the subject project will qualify for the reduced GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent each of CGST & SGST), as provided in Sl. No. 3, item (v), sub-item (da) of Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

HELD: From a reading of the clarification, notification and the clause (da) of item (v) of Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) and facts on record, it is found that that applicant's case is covered under concessional tax rate of 12 per cent, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services) in terms of item (v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017, dated 28-6-2017 as amended, since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing Project'. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to applicant in the cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018 i.e. the date on which Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of said reduced rate would be applicable in case of only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. In case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. or commercial units, the applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate, since the benefit of reduced rate is available only for residential units of carpet area less than 60 sq. mtrs. [Para 5.11]

the rate of tax applicable to the transaction of the applicant and more so whether the transactions are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended). The applicant himself has clearly stated that his transactions are not covered under entry No. 3(ii) of the said notification and hence they are not considered as the same is also agreed by this Authority. [Para 11.4] The Entry No.3(vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No.24/2017- Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017), reads as under:

'(vi) Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of -

(a)

a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

(b)

a structure meant predominantly for use as (i) an educational, (ii) clinical, or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or

(c)

a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of Schedule III of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.'

and the condition stated in the Column (5) of the Notification is 'Provided that where the services are supplied to a Government Entity, they should have been procured by the said entity in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or local authority, as the case maybe.'[Para 11.5]

The Government Entity is defined in clause (x) of paragraph 4 of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, (as amended) to mean an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation,

(i)

set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

established by any Government,

with 90 per cent. or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 11.6]

For a works contract to be covered under this entry, the following conditions needs to be satisfied:

(a)

The recipient of services must be a Government Entity and in this case, Bangalore Development Authority;

(b)

The works contract services supplied by the main contractor must be in relation to the works covered under (a), (b) or (c);

(c)

The recipient of such services must have procured these services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or local authority. [Para 11.7]

Regarding the first question, Bangalore Development Authority is an authority established by the State Government under the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 and it is entrusted with the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith. [Para 11.8]

It is very clear from section 3(3) of the BDA Act that the control over the entity rests with the Government of Karnataka and hence the Bangalore Development Authority satisfies both the conditions and hence is considered as a Government Entity within the meaning of the Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 11.9]

Regarding the second question, whether the services provided by the main contractor are covered under clauses (a), (b) or (c) of the entry No.3(vi) of the said Notification, the following are noticed:[Para 11.10]

The applicant is constructing a Housing Project at two places in around Bangalore on subcontract basis rewarded from GIEPL. The Bangalore Development Authority in its tender has stated that it has taken up construction of housing in and around Bangalore City as designed by the Government of Karnataka. Since this is a residential project for general public, the same is not covered under clause (b) or (c). [Para 11.10.1]

The projects of the applicant are involving the supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and hence is a 'works contract' within the meaning of section 2(119) of CGST Act. This works contract is for a construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, the works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and hence it is covered under clause (a) of the entry 3(vi) of the Notification, subject to the conditions. [Para 11.10.2]

supply and the works are not naturally bundled. It cannot be a mixed supply also because the valuations of each of the supply of works are valued separately and they would amount to separate contracts. Hence, there is no common price for all the contracts. Hence, it can be decided that each of the works mentioned in a schedule is a separate contract in itself and this is bolstered by the fact that the works are not in the same place and also are different in nature. [Para 15] Thus, the new constructions involved in the contract are liable to tax at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST) as per entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 20/2017 - Central tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017. The services of repairs, maintenance, renovation and alterations of residential complex meant for use of the Railway employees are covered under entry 3(vi) of the notification and, hence, eligible for tax at 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST. Other repair works of old construction involved in the contract are liable to tax at 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST) as per entry No.3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time-to-time. [Para 16]

In case of other flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs. or commercial units, the applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate, since the benefit of reduced rate is available only for residential units of carpet area less than 60 sq. mtrs. [Para 5.11] The applicant's submission that entry (v)(da) of Notification 1/2018, mentioned above nowhere restricts the benefit to a 'Developer' only is accepted. The Notification entry is qua the supply of service and not qua the person and therefore once a project qualifies as an Affordable Housing Project, the benefit of concessional rate of tax would be available in respect of works contract services pertaining to Low Cost Houses, irrespective of it being supplied by the Developer or the Contractor. In the subject case, the project qualifies as an Affordable Housing Project, and the benefit of concessional rate of tax at the rate of 12 per cent GST, would thus be available to the applicant. [Para 5.12]

Another question raised by applicant is whether the building completion and finishing services be regarded as a separate service or would it be a composite supply of works contract service as covered under entry (v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 to avail the benefit of reduced rate of tax. [Para 5.13]

It is seen that the terms entered into between the applicant and developer is for a composite supply of works contract which includes the supply of building, completion and finishing services. Supply of these services are pertaining to original work. The applicant's contention that the building completion and finishing services cannot be treated as a separate service since the contract envisages that the said services would be provided as a part and parcel of the main activity which is, construction of dwelling units, is accepted. [Para 5.13.2]

In view of the terms of the contract, it is opined that building completion and finishing services would not be regarded as separate services. It would be a part of the composite supply of works contract services rendered by the applicant with principal supply of building construction and in view of the discussions made above, supply of finishing services will be covered under entry (v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 and applicant will be eligible to avail the benefit of reduced rate of tax i.e. 12 per cent ,only in respect of dwelling units having area less than 60 sq. mtrs. [Para 5.13.3]

Another question comes up for determination is what would be the appropriate rate of Goods and Services Tax on works contract services provided for the construction of the units and common areas and amenities on pro rate basis which do not qualify the criteria of low cost houses. [Para 5.14]

There is no doubt that the project undertaken by the applicant pertains to an affordable housing project. In the subject project, the applicant will be constructing dwelling units of less than 60 sq. mtrs. carpet area as well as dwelling units having carpet area greater than 60 sq. mtrs. [Para 5.14.1]

It is found that common amenities form part of the overall construction service and are always naturally bundled when offered to the customer. Therefore, such services will qualify as composite supply of works contract service, where the principal supply would be, construction services. Accordingly, the rate applicable to the principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities. The word 'housing project' cannot be confined only to dwelling units, it would also include within its fold, other common amenities, structures, etc. Common amenities form part of the overall construction service and are always naturally bundled when offered to the customer. Therefore, such services will qualify as composite supply of works contract service wherein provision of construction services is the principal supply. Accordingly, the rate applicable to the principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities i.e. in respect of dwelling units having area less than 60 sq. mtrs., the GST rate would be 12 per cent and in cases of dwelling units having area greater than 60 sq. mtrs. the GST rate would be 18 per cent. [Para 5.14.2]

It is held that the applicant's case is covered under the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land), under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v)(da) of above mentioned Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing'. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in the cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018 i.e., the date on which Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable only in case of amenities pertaining to only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. In case of amenities provided to purchasers of flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs., the applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate i.e. at the rate of 18 per cent GST. [Para 5.14]

No. 3(i) to 3(if) or 3(xii) as the supply made by them to the intended buyer is a composite supply of works contract and not a construction simpliciter and the other entries which provides for 'Composite supply of works contract' do not apply to them. In view of the foregoing, it is ruled that the Proposed Modus operandi for construction of 'Unit' which is 'other than affordable residential apartments' by the applicant in the RREP promoted by them, namely, 'Ashiana Shubam -Phase IV' in Chennai is classifiable under SAC 9954 as 'Construction Service' and the applicable rate of tax is CGST at the rate of 3.75 per cent and SGST at the rate of 3.75 per cent as per Entry Sl. HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Kerala State Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)- Section 2(119), of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per tender requirements - They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for construction of a building for space transportation system - It is a composite contract which includes supply of materials as well as service - They have also received another work order from Infrastructure Kerala Ltd., a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for development of Medical College which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Applicant has requested for advance ruling on rate of tax applicable for above works contracts awarded by Government authorities - Whether since services provided by applicant under both contracts fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services are being provided to Central Government and State Government, applicant is eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Held, yes [Para 9]GST: Where services of construction with material provided by applicant under construction contracts awarded by Government authorities fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services being provided to Central and State government, applicant will be eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3 (vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017, dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The applicant is carrying on business in the housing and construction sector. They are engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per the tender requirements. They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for the construction of a building for space transportation system. It is a composite contract which includes supply of materials as well as service. They have also received another work order from a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for the development of Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure.

The applicant has requested for advance ruling on the rate of tax applicable for the above works contracts awarded by the Government authorities.

HELD: As per section 2(119), 'works contract' means a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.[Para 5]

On a perusal of the work orders and the agreements entered by the applicant it is clear that the services rendered by the applicant clearly falls within the definition of works contract under section 2(119).[Para 6]

Since the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts fall under the definition of works contract under section 2(119) and the services being provided to the Central Government and State Government, the applicant is eligible for the concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended.

In view of the observations stated above, it is ruled that the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts being composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 provided to the Central Government and State Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry or any other business or profession is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended and attract GST at the rate of 12 per cent [6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST].

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Section 7 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 7 of the Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Supply - Scope of - Applicant is a developer of Residential Real Estate Project (RREP) - It has launched a senior-living gated community project in Chennai by acquiring development rights from Landowner back in 2014 - Applicant as a POA of Landowner, along with Landowner entered into 'Agreement for Sale' and 'Indenture of Understanding" with prospective buyer of a Unit of developed Project and entered into a 'Construction Agreement' with such buyer exclusively - Whether applicant being a Promoter of approved RREP, construction of a 'Unit' which is other than affordable residential apartments in said RREP is an activity of Construction of part of building with intention for sale - Held, yes - Whether therefore, supply of service of construction of a 'Unit' in RERP - Phase IV, based on 'Construction agreement' entered into by applicant with prospective buyer intended for sale to buyer, is a 'Supply of Construction service' and classification of service as per 'Scheme of Classification of Service' is 'Construction Service under SAC 9954' and it will not be classified under SAC 9997 as claimed by applicant - Held, yes - Whether applicable rate of tax on said project will be CGST at rate of 3.75 per cent and SGST at rate of 3.75 per cent as per Entry Sl. No. 3 (ia) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Held, yes [Paras 8.5, 8.7, 9.2 and 10]GST : GST on construction of unit which is other than affordable residential apartments by applicant in Residential Real Estate Project (RREP) promoted by them is classifiable under SAC 9954 as 'Construction Service' and applicable rate of tax is 7 per cent GST

FACT: The applicant is a real estate developer who has launched a senior-living gated community project called 'Ashiana Shubham' in Chennai by acquiring development rights from Landowner back in 2014. The applicant as a POA of the Landowner, along with the Landowner entered into 'Agreement for Sale' and 'Indenture of Understanding' with the prospective buyer of a Unit of the developed Project and also entered into a 'Construction Agreement' with such buyer exclusively.

The project is divided into 5 phases. Phase I was completed in pre-GST regime, Phase II completed in GST regime, Phase III commenced prior to 1-4-2019 and is scheduled to be completed in 2022. Phase IV is scheduled to be launched soon and Phase V will be launched in future. It is stated that they have initiated the process of acquiring the necessary approvals from Tamil Nadu RERA, required for launching Phase IV and the applicant has furnished the acknowledgement receipt of submission of application to Tamil Nadu RERA dated 19-10-2020 and the Director of Town Planning's approval for Phase IV.

The applicant sought advance ruling on whether the activities of construction carried out by the applicant for its customer under the Construction Agreement, being composite supply of works contract are appropriately classifiable under Heading 9997, and chargeable to CGST at the rate of 9 per cent under Sl. No. 35 of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017?

or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or

(c)

a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule III of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The applicant is engaged in construction work of office building for APSFC, which is meant for governance of corporation activities. The applicant is of the view that the use of the said construction (building) is not for any business or so. As seen from the Annual Reports for the years 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18 as made available by APSFC in its website, it is engaged in providing financial services to industries and entrepreneurs. The income it is getting is from interest on loans and advances and also service charges, upfront fee/commitment fee, sale of application forms, profit on sale of assets, commission on insurance, rent received, etc. Therefore, the activities of APSFC are business activities and not otherwise. The applicant informed that the said building is for use as office by APSFC. Therefore, it appears that the said construction is for office use for conducting business activities of APSFC. Moreover the applicant did not provide any information or documentary proof evidencing that the construction/building is for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession to be eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) available under Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017.

In the instant case, the contract entered by the applicant is classifiable under Heading No. 9954 under construction services and it falls under entry (ii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, i.e., composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under Central Tax and 9 per cent under State Tax).

Ruling

The activity of the applicant under the agreement with APSFC is a composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The APSFC is a Government Entity within the meaning of para 4 of clause (x) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017.

As the use of the construction/building is for office purpose of APSFC to conduct its activities which are not other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession, the concessional rate of 12 per cent under Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 read with Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 is not available to the applicant.

The activities under the agreement referred by the applicant are classifiable under Heading No. 9954 under construction services and they fall under entry (ii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and the applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent Central Tax plus 9 per cent State Tax).

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Construction services (NR) - Applicant, a partnership firm of builders and developers is to undertake an affordable housing project on their land - It seeks advance ruling on what is rate of tax to be levied on sale of flats/units to prospective buyers - According to sub-item (da) of item (v) of Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate) 25-1-2018, low-cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house is an affordable housing project which has been given infrastructure status vide notification of Government of India - Whether since project undertaken by applicant falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing project' concessional rate of taxes to be levied is 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) - Held, yes [Para 5]GST: Rate of tax to be levied is 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) in case of Affordable Housing Project  GST : Where concessional rate of tax of 12 per cent on affordable housing project is levied by GST Council, builder or developer having paid GST of 18 per cent or 28 per cent on inputs and capital goods used in construction of flats, will not be required to pay GST on construction service of flats, etc., as they would have enough ITC (input tax credits) in their books to pay output GST

Section 16 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Input tax credit - Eligibility and condition for taking credits (NR) - GST Council has extended concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sq. mtrs. in a affordable housing project - Whether, consequently, builder or developer having paid GST of 18 per cent or 28 per cent on inputs and capital goods used in construction of flats, will not be required to pay GST on construction service of flats, etc., in cash as they would have enough ITC (input tax credits) in their books to pay output GST; further, they should not recover any GST payable on flats from buyers - Held, yes [Para 5]

FACT: The applicant-firm of builders and developers is desirous to undertake an affordable housing project in Kolhapur. The land required for the project is already possessed by the firm. The units to be constructed in the said project will be of upto 30 sq. mtrs. (EWS) or upto 60 sq. mtrs. (LIG). It seeks advance ruling as to what is the rate of tax to be levied on the sale of Flats/Units to the prospective buyers? and whether full ITC is allowable or it will be restricted to out put GST liability?

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Andhra Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of office building - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant has entered into an agreement with Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation for construction of office building - Whether activities undertaken by applicant are classifiable under Heading No. 9954, i.e., under entry (ii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent Central Tax + 9 per cent State Tax) - Held, yes [Para 5] [In favour of revenue]GST: Where applicant has entered into an agreement with Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation for construction of office building, activities undertaken by applicant are classifiable under Heading No. 9954 under construction services

FACT: The applicant has entered into an agreement with Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation for construction of office building.

It sought advance ruling on applicable rate of tax under GST for construction of office building for Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation.

HELD: Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation (APSFC) is a term lending institution established in 1956 for promoting small and medium scale industries in Andhra Pradesh under the provisions of the State Financial Corporation Act, 1951. The functions of the corporation are to launch entrepreneur friendly schemes to provide term loans, working capital term loans, special and seed capital assistance, etc.

The APSFC is established by the Government and the Government of Andhra Pradesh is having more than 90 per cent of control over it. Thus it is covered under the definition of 'Government Entity'. Therefore, the APSFC is a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST matters.

The applicant agreed for construction of office building to APSFC, which includes procurement and supply of goods and services for agreed consideration. The activity of construction includes both supply of goods and also services.

Section 2(119) defines 'works contract' as a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alternation or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.

The composite supply of works contract under section 2(119) is treated as supply of service in terms of Serial No. 6(a) of Schedule II of the CGST Act.

The Government of India vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 notified the rate of GST applicable on supply of services. Under this Notification for Heading No. 9954, the applicable rate of GST is 9 per cent.

Vide Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017, Government of India by inserting entry (vi) notified concessional GST rate of 6 per cent for the construction services provided to Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority or a Governmental Authority by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of —

(a)

a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

(b)

a structure meant predominantly for use as (i) an educational, (ii) a clinical, or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or

(c)

a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule III of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The applicant is engaged in construction work of office building for APSFC, which is meant for governance of corporation activities. The applicant is of the view that the use of the said construction (building) is not for any business or so.

No. 3 of the said notification. [Para 7] The first question of the applicant is regarding the rate of tax on the services of construction of different types of residential apartments in the project rendered to their customers during the period from 1-7-2017 to 31-3-2019. From the facts as disclosed by the applicant in the application, it is evident that the ongoing residential project does not fall under any of the schemes of affordable housing projects listed in Sl. No. 3 and hence the services of construction of residential apartments in the project rendered by the applicant do not qualify for the concessional rate of tax of 12 per cent under any of the sub-tems or items of Sl. No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. Therefore, the services of construction of all different types of residential apartments in the project is liable to GST at the rate of 18 per cent [ 9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST] as per Item (I) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 8]

The second question raised by the applicant is regarding the taxable value of services for the period 1-7-2017 onwards for which appropriation towards undivided share of land was already done in pre-GST period and whether the one-third deduction as provided for in para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017 can again be taken where the value of undivided share already appropriated is lower than one-third of the total amount receivable for project including land value. On a plain reading of provision of para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017, it is evident that the taxable value of service specified at Item (i) of the said notification is the total amount charged for the supply less the value of land or undivided share of land and the value of land or undivided share of land shall be deemed to be one third of the total amount charged for the supply. Therefore, the value of land or undivided share of land is deemed to be one-third of the total amount charged for the supply irrespective of the actual value of land and, accordingly, the applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of the total amount charged for the supply in arriving at the taxable value of the supply. [Para 9]

The third question raised by the applicant is regarding the applicable rate of tax for the period after 1-4-2019 where option was already exercised in respect of the apartments mentioned therein and eligibility for one-third deduction to the extent consideration for undivided share of land is also included. Consequent to the introduction of the new tax structure for real estate sector with effect from 1-4-2019 onwards by amendment of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 by Notification No. 3/2019 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 the applicant has opted for continuing payment of tax at the old rates that have been specified in item (ie) or (if) of the said notification in respect of the services of construction of residential apartments in the ongoing project. The project does not come under any of the schemes specified in item (ie) of the said notification and accordingly the services of construction of the residential apartments in the project is liable to GST for the period from 1-4-2019 at the rate of 18 per cent [9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST] as per item (if) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2019 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 in accordance with the option exercised by the applicant. The item (if) of Sl. No. 3 of the said notification provides that the provisions of paragraph 2 of the notification shall apply for valuation of the service. Therefore, the applicant is eligible for deduction of one-third of the total amount charged for the supply in determining the taxable value of such supply after 1-4-2019 also. [Para 10]

In case of amenities provided to purchasers of flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs., the applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate i.e. at the rate of 18 per cent GST. [Para 5.14] Subject project consists of both, dwelling units less than and also greater than 60 sq. mtrs. Benefit of concessional rate is only available to 'Affordable Housing' as already discussed above. The definition of 'Affordable Housing' is confined to dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 square meters. Thus, concessional rate available to applicant is only in respect of low cost houses along with amenities constructed by the applicant. The common amenities and areas are a part of 'Affordable Housing Project' and therefore the applicant will be entitled to benefit of concessional rate for the same, only when they are a part of low cost houses, i.e. units less than 60 sq. mtrs. The applicant will thus have to discharge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (after deducting value of land) on works contract services provided for the construction of the units and common areas and amenities, which do qualify the criteria of low cost houses. Since concessional rate would be available only for construction services pertaining to dwelling units less than 60 sq. mtrs. Including common areas and amenities on pro rata basis, construction services including common areas and amenities on pro rata basis, performed by the applicant in respect of dwelling units exceeding 60 sq. mtrs. would be liable to full rate of GST, i.e., 18 per cent.
