HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - A charitable organisation 'S' engaged in various charitable activities across Kerala has awarded a rehabilitation project to applicant for providing affordable shelter to 2018 flood victims - Applicant constructed 45 residential units in different locations on land belonging to flood victims identified by Trust - Whether activity undertaken by applicant cannot be construed as construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer and, hence, rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is not applicable in respect of said activity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant is construction of 45 individual residential houses at different locations on land belonging to individual beneficiaries and activity squarely falls within scope of works contract as defined in section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether services provided by applicant to 'S' for construction of low cost housing units falls within ambit of Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 15]GST : Where applicant constructed residential units on land belonging to flood victims under a rehabilitation project awarded to it by a charitable trust, activity squarely falls within scope of works contract under section 2(119) and is liable to GST at rate of 12 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The applicant is a non-governmental organization in the shelter sector having sustainable building solutions and green and humane architecture.

It is providing services in the field of construction of residences and affordable housing, architectural advisory services, execution of government contracts etc. with special focus on environment friendly construction.

A charitable organisation 'S' engaged in various charitable activities across Kerala has awarded a rehabilitation project to the applicant for providing affordable shelter to the 2018 flood victims.

The applicant is awarded the work of construction of 45 residential units ad-measuring approximately equal to or less than 450 Square feet in different locations each along with residential facilities on the land belonging to the flood victims identified by the Trust. The applicant shall design the houses, obtain the statutory permits and construct the houses and hand them over on a turnkey basis.

The applicant has sought advance ruling on the question as to whether the services provided by the applicant to 'S' for construction of low cost housing units for flood-affected individuals in Kerala fall within the ambit of Serial Number 3 (i), (v) or (va) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 03/2019 Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and whether services by the applicant are otherwise exempt from whole or part of GST leviable thereon by Notification 12/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended.

HELD: The rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 applies to construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer except where the entire consideration is received after issuance of completion certificate. Further, the rate under this entry applies where the supply of the services involves transfer of land or undivided share of land and its value is included in the amount charged from the buyer. [Para 8]

The activity undertaken by the applicant for 'S' as per the agreement dated 16-11-2019 cannot by any stretch of imagination be construed as construction of affordable residential apartments by a promoter in a residential real estate project intended for sale to a buyer and, hence, the rate of GST prescribed under Sl. No. 3(i) of the Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 03/2019 Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 is not applicable in respect of the activity. The activity undertaken by the applicant is construction of 45 individual residential houses at different locations on the land belonging to the individual beneficiaries and the activity squarely falls within the scope of works contract as defined in section 2(119). [Para 11]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction service provided to National Centre for Biological Sciences - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant has entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences [NCBS] for purpose of execution of works contract for construction of building at NCBS Campus - NCBS is not Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity - Whether service supplied by applicant to NCBS is covered under item (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and taxable at 9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST - Held, yes [Para 6] [In favour of revenue]GST : Where applicant has entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences [NCBS] for purpose of execution of works contract for construction of building at NCBS Campus, service supplied by applicant to NCBS is covered under item (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and taxable at 9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST

FACT: The applicant has entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences [NCBS] for the purpose of execution of works contract for construction of building for laboratories and associated facilities at NCBS Campus in Bangalore.

It sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

What is the applicable rate of tax for the provision of construction service rendered to NCBS.

HELD: The applicant is providing works contract service to NCBS and there is no dispute whatsoever that it is a works contract service as per clause (119) of section 2. [Para 5.2]

The NCBS has obtained registration under the GST Act as a trust and the council managing this organisation has three members appointed by the Government of India, one member appointed by the Government of Maharashtra, two members appointed by the trustees of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, the Director of the Institute (NCBS) is an ex-officio member and one co-opted member appointed by the council. Hence four members are from the Government. [Para 5.3]

The issue is whether the NCBS is covered under any one of the categories viz. Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. It is clear at the outset itself that NCBS is not Central Government or State Government or Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 5.4]

The argument of the applicant that the NCBS is covered under the category Government Authority cannot be accepted in the light of the definition of Governmental Authority in clause (ix) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017). [Para 5.5]

The only question that needs to be examined is whether NCBS is a Government Entity or not. Clause (x) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017) defines Government Entity as:

'Government Entity' means an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation,

(i)

Set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

Established by any Government,

with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 5.6]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Construction services) - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant is engaged in development and construction of residential and commercial complex, called 'SAMANVAY RESIDENCY' - Development Authority has approved 'Samnvay Residency' under 'Affordable Housing Project' - Whether since project undertaken by applicant falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing', applicant's case is covered under reduced tax rate of 12 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 18-22]GST : Where applicant is engaged in development of residential project called 'SAMANVAY RESIDENCY', which falls under affordable housing project, construction services provided by applicant qualifies for reduced tax rate of 12 per cent GST as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The applicant, engaged in business of construction of residential and commercial complex, is developing residential project called 'SAMANVAY RESIDENCY'.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether the construction services provided by the applicant under the project 'SAMANVAY RESIDENCY' qualifies for the reduced CGST rate of 6 per cent (under CGST and SGST Act) as provided in Sl. No. 3 item (v) sub-item (da) of Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

HELD: According to sub-item (da) of item (v) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, low-cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house in an affordable housing project, which has been given infrastructure status vide notification of Government of India, in Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs vide F. No. 13/6/2009- INF, dated the 30-3-2017 would attract a tax rate of 12 per cent. This clause will be applicable to the applicant if the project undertaken by them is an affordable housing project which has been given infrastructure status vide Government of India notification. [Para 17.2]

Department of Economic Affairs' in the Notification issued vide F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated 30-3-2017, has included Affordable Housing under the column "Infrastructure sub-sector" against the category of Social and Commercial Infrastructure. In the said notification, term "Affordable Housing" has been defined as a housing project using at least 50 per cent of the Floor Area Ratio (FAR)/Floor Space Index (FSI) for dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 square meters. Further, in the said Notification, it is mentioned that 'Carpet Area' shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (k) of section 2 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. [Para 18]

One of the recommendations made by the GST Council in its 25th meeting held on 18th January, 2018 at Delhi was to extend the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) to services by way of construction of low cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 sqmt. in a housing project, which has been given infrastructure status under Notification No. 13/06/2009 dated 30-3-2009. The said notification of Department of Economic Affairs provides infrastructure status to Affordable Housing. The recommendation of the Council would extend the concessional rate to construction of flats/houses of less than 60 sqmt. in projects other than the projects covered by any scheme of the Central or State Government also. [Para 20]

The applicant has during the personal hearing submitted that land on which the project "Samnvay Residency" was constructed is free hold land not having any common area of facility in respect of any other land or Residential or Commercial project. Further, Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority has approved "Samnvay Residency" under the "Affordable Housing Project" and Architect has given certificate that land area of the said scheme is 3465 Sq. Mtrs. This scheme is having total 5 blocks. The total FSI of the scheme is 9342.61 Sq. Mtrs. and out of which 9084.81 Sq. Mtr. of FSI consumed in the flats having carpet area below 60 Sq. Mtrs. [Para 21.1]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No.9954 (Construction services) - Construction service is provided by applicant contractor under project 'La-Riveria' - Apartment in said project is less than 60 sq. mt. carpet area - Whether said project is an affordable housing project which qualifies for application of lower rate of CGST of 6 per cent and SGST at rate of 6 per cent w.e.f. 25-1-2018 as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Held, yes [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]GST: Construction service provided by applicant contractor under project 'La-Riveria', which is an affordable housing project, qualifies for application of lower rate of CGST of 6 per cent and SGST of 6 per cent w.e.f. 25-1-2018 as provided in Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended vide Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018

FACT: The applicant has been undertaking development of residential project 'La-Riveria'. The apartments in project La-Riveria are less than 60 sq. mt. RERA carpet area.

It seeks ruling on application of GST on said services.

HELD: The applicant has not been given the entire contract for construction of complete houses. Probably the carpentry work like making of doors, etc., electrical work, etc., does not seem to have been given to them. However, the job alloted to them are pertaining to affordable housing since each of the apartments is less than 60 sq. mtrs. Entry (V)(da) of Notification 1/2018, nowhere restricts the benefit to a 'developer' only. The Notification entry is qua the supply of service and not qua the person and, therefore, once a project qualifies as an Affordable Housing Project (AHP), the benefit of concessional rate of tax would be available in respect of works contract services pertaining to Low Cost Houses, irrespective of it being supplied by the developer or the contractor. Hence, in view of the above discussion and facts on record the applicant's case is covered under the tax rate of 12 per cent, under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (V)(da) of abovementioned Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing' as also claimed by them in their application. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in the case of supply effected after 25-1-2018, i.e., the date on which Notification 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable in case of only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs., in this scheme, which is covered in the category of affodable housing. [Para 5]

HEADNOTE: Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Installation, commissioning and fitting out of a civil structure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Department of Space, Government of India entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Thiruvananthapuram - Work involves aerodynamic structural and control design analysis, detailed design, detailed engineering, fabrication, procurement, inspection, third party inspection, loading and unloading of material, transportation to site, civil and electrical works, integration of systems, training, documentation, acceptance, testing and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel - Whether supply under contract can be considered as supply of equipment eligible for concessional rate of GST as per Sl. No. 243B of Schedule I of Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, no - Whether work of design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract - Held, yes - Whether service provided by applicant to Central Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 6] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Where Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel, supply under contract cannot be considered as supply of equipment and work as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract and service provided by applicant will attract 12 per cent GST

FACT: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Department of Space, Government of India entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Thiruvananthapuram. The work involves aerodynamic structural and control design analysis, detailed design, detailed engineering, fabrication, procurement, inspection, third party inspection, loading and unloading of material, transportation to site, civil and electrical works, integration of systems, training, documentation, acceptance, testing and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel.

The applicant sought advance ruling on the following questions:

1.

Whether the supply under the contract for Design, Realization, Integration and Commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, ISRO, Thiruvananthapuram can be considered as supply of equipment eligible for the concessional rate of GST under Sl. No. 243A of Schedule I of Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2018.

2.

If the above supply is considered as works contract whether it would be covered under Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017) attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent.

HELD: As per Sl. No. 243B of Schedule I of Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, the scientific and technical instruments, apparatus, equipments, accessories, parts and components, spares and tools, mock ups and modules, raw materials and consumables required for launch vehicles and satellite and payloads has been granted concessional rate of GST of 5 per cent. This entry does not include installation, commissioning and fitting out of a civil structure as the concessional rate of tax is given only to the scientific and technical instruments, apparatus, etc. [Para 3]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant is promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing a residential house project named 'Akriti' (RREP) - Whether works contract service received from contractors for construction of those dwelling units in project named 'Akriti' that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of said notification, provided applicant does not opt for paying tax at rate specified in Entry No. 3(ie) or Entry No. 3(if) - Held, yes [Para 4.10]GST : Where applicant who is promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing residential housing project 'Akriti', works contract service received from contractors for construction of those dwelling units that are affordable residential apartments in terms of clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) are taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of said notification, provided applicant does not opt for paying tax at rate specified in Entry No. 3(ie) Entry No. 3(if)

FACT: The applicant is the promoter of residential real estate project, supplying construction service in developing a residential housing project named 'Akriti' (RREP).

The applicant wants to know whether Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (Rate Notification), as amended time-to-time, applies to the works contract service received from the contractors.

HELD: Entry No. 3(v)(da) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is related to the construction of low-cost apartments. Clause (xvi) of Paragraph 4 of the Rate Notification defines an affordable residential apartment. It shall mean a residential apartment in a project which commences on or after 1-4-2019 or in an ongoing project in respect of which the promoter has not exercised the option to pay tax at the rate specified in (ie) or (if) of Entry No. 3, having carpet area not exceeding 60 sq. mtr. in metropolitan cities or 90 sq. mtr. In cities or towns other than metropolitan cities and for which the gross amount charged is not more than 45 lakhs. [Para 4.1]

The flats having a carpet area of 60 sq. mtr. or less per unit in the RREP qualify as affordable residential apartments, provided the gross amount charged per unit does not exceed Rs. 45 lakhs and the promoter has not exercised the option to pay tax at the rate specified in (ie) or (if) of Entry No. 3. It now needs to be ascertained whether the RREP is an affordable housing project, which enjoys infrastructure status vide the AHP Notification. [Para 4.6]

Affordable housing has been defined in the AHP Notification as a housing project using at least 50 per cent of FAR/FSI for dwelling units with a carpet area of not more than 60 sq. mtr. The term 'carpet area' has been assigned the same meaning as in section 2(k) of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. It means the net usable floor area of an apartment, excluding the area covered by the external walls, areas under services shafts, balcony or veranda and open terrace, but includes the area covered by the internal partition walls of the apartment. [Para 4.7]

The Floor Area Ratio (FAR), also known as the Floor Space Ratio (FSR) or the Floor Space Index (FSI), depicts the relationship between the total usable floor space in a building and the total area of the plot on which the building is constructed. In mathematical terms, FAR = CA/LA, where CA = Constructed area or built-up area, and LA = Land area. [Para 4.8]

The Floor Area Ratio (FAR), also known as the Floor Space Ratio (FSR) or the Floor Space Index (FSI), depicts the relationship between the total usable floor space in a building and the total area of the plot on which the building is constructed. In mathematical terms, FAR = CA/LA, where CA = Constructed area or built-up area, and LA = Land area. [Para 4.8] According to the Project Plan submitted at the time of the hearing, FAR for the entire project is 2.749 after deducting from the total built-up area the common areas like lift-lobby, stair area etc. FAR for the affordable residential apartments in the project should, therefore, be atleast 1.375. This issue is with respect to the housing project called 'Prajapati Magnum' in Dronagiri, Navi Mumbai which has been undertaken by them. The applicant has submitted that the said project was started in December 2013 and is expected to be completed in December 2022. They have also submitted that the total FSI consumed in the said project is 18,099.50 sq. mtrs out of which 13,145.26 sq. mtrs of FSI are consumed for flats having carpet area below 60 sq. mtrs. They have, whilst submitting Architect's Certificate in support, submitted that their housing project is using around 73 per cent of the total Floor Area Ratio (FAR)/Floor Space Index and therefore their project falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing' as mentioned in notification issued by Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs vide F. No. 13/6/2009-INF, dated the 30-3-2017.

Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in Column 3 of the Table in the said Notification, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein.

applicant and for this very reason, 'construction of a complex or building or a part..' is specifically mentioned to be treated as 'Supply of Service' under Para 5(b) of the Schedule II of the ACT. Thus, in the facts of the case, the applicant being a Promoter of the approved RREP, the construction of a 'Unit' in the said RREP is an activity of Construction of part of the building with the intention for sale. [Para 8.5] Coming to the classification of the service, the Scheme of Classification of Services under GST is as per the Annexure to Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate) and the applicable rates of GST are provided in the 'Table' of the Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate) which is based on the description of service given in Column (3) corresponding to the Heading specified in Column (2) of the Table of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended. 'Works contract' is not defined as a separate service in the Annexure to the Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate) but the service descriptions at Column (3) mentions 'Composite supply of Works Contract' in many of the entries. The classification of service may be construction, erection, commissioning, etc., of the immovable property and the contract for execution may be a works contract, in which, while providing the service, there is a transfer of property in goods. The mode of supply does not determine the classification of service. Classification of service is to be done based on the Scheme of Classification and there is no reason to agree to the contention of the applicant that the service provided by them is not classifiable under SAC 9954. The applicant contends that their activity is classifiable under SAC 9997, which is falling under section 9 which constitutes activities relating to community, social and personal services and other miscellaneous services. It can be seen that Heading 9954 under section 5 of the scheme of classification covers 'Construction Services' and is a specific entry. Heading 9997 under section 9 of the Scheme of classification covers 'Other services-Other Miscellaneous service' and in that section, SAC 999799- other services nowhere else classified would naturally hold services in relation to the main heading which is community, Social or personal services. In the instant case, the applicant develops RREP along with all the infra structures and constructs the 'Units' of the RREP, i.e., construction of single/multiple dwelling unit and as such it clearly falls under construction services and the contention of the applicant to classify the same under 9997 is thus not entertainable and not tenable under law. Further it may be noted that even when a service is capable of differential treatment for any purpose based on its description, the most specific description shall be preferred over a more general description. In the instant case, the most specific description being construction services, the subject activity falls under the SAC 9954 and therefore, the classification of service is 'Construction Service' only, for the purpose of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended. [Para 8.6]

In view of the above, it is held that, the supply of service of construction of a 'Unit' in the RREP- Phase IV, based on the 'Construction agreement' entered into by the applicant, engaged in the Development of the said RREP, with the prospective buyer intended for sale to the buyer, is a ' Supply of Construction service' and the classification of the service as per the 'Scheme of Classification of Service' is 'Construction Service under SAC 9954' and it will not be classified under SAC 9997 as claimed by the applicant. [Para 8.7]

The rate of tax applicable for the SAC 9954 is given under Sl. No. 3(i), (ia), (ib), (ic), (id), (ie), (if), (iii), (iv), (v), (va), (vi), (vii), (viii), (ix), (x), (xi) and (xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 03/2019 dated 29-3-2019. It is found that the applicant has stated to have considered the entries and concluded that their supply is not covered under Sl. No. 3(i) to 3(if) or 3(xii) as the supply made by them to the intended buyer is a composite supply of works contract and not a construction simpliciter and the other entries which provides for 'Composite supply of works contract' do not apply to them. [Para 9.1]

HELD: There are number of works entrusted by IIT Bhubaneswar to the applicant under a single contract/agreement made on 2-5-2016. It is also found that IIT,Bhubaneswar has engaged the applicant as a 'Project Management Consultant'. In order to execute the project, the applicant has engaged contractors through different competitive tender process. The applicant has awarded different types of works to various agencies/contractors with categorical mention of individual works to be carried out by them with specific remuneration for each such work. Hence, it is a supply having distinctly identifiable components with distinct value attributable to each of the components. However, the contention of the applicant cannot be agreed with for the reasons that the items covered under the 'Scope of Work' are disjoint in character and can be supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business. Hence, the views of the applicant that the supply of services and goods encompassed in the subject work order/contract are naturally bundled cannot be accepted. Mere fact that a number of tasks have been entrusted to the applicant would not make it entitled to be categorised as 'composite supply' particularly in terms of section 2(30). [Para 4.2]

The applicant has stated that IIT, Bhubaneswar has been established by the Government. All the institutions of the Indian Institutes of Technology are established by the Government of India, Ministry of Human Resource Development. Further, IITs under the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) are the institutions controlled and owned by the Ministry of Human Resource Development. That being the stated position, IIT, Bhubaneswar is entitled to be termed as 'Government Entity' in terms of Explanation to Notification No. 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate), and also as per Notification No. 31/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 13-10-2017. The issue of IIT, Bhubaneswar being a Government entity has been stated with at length in the application submitted by the Applicant. 'Government Entity' is defined in the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax rate vide clause 4(x). [Para 4.3]

Government of India, Ministry of Human Resource Development is exercising full control over the activities of IITs all over the country. In the given circumstance IIT, Bhubaneswar qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST law, as it fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions laid down under notification supra. It therefore leaves no doubt that IIT, Bhubaneswar is a Government Entity for the purpose of provisions of CGST Act, 2017 and OGST Act, 2017. [Para 4.4]

Entry No. 3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (R) covers a wide spectrum of Construction Services as composite supply. [Para 4.5]

In the instant case it is found that the applicant has been engaged as a PMC to execute the contract for carrying out different specified works for IIT, Bhubaneswar which includes erection, commissioning, installation, etc. It is also found that for executing the project, the applicant shall be paid agency charges of 5.5 per cent in addition to the actual cost of work. The agency charges are type of commission or remuneration for rendering 'consulting service' to IIT, Bhubaneswar. It is also found to be necessary to place on record that there are certain items of supply made to IIT, Bhubaneswar including, but not limited to, 'supply of consulting services' which definitely do not find place in the ambit of Sr. No. 3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate). Needless to mention that such supply shall not qualify for exemption as envisaged under Sr. No. 3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate), inasmuch as the said supply is a 'Pure Service' and not in the nature of works contract service. [Para 4.6]

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Applicant is awarded a contract with Railways for new building of railway station, repair work, addition and alteration to existing structure - Whether other repair works of old construction involved in contract are liable to tax at 18 per cent as per Entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 16]

FACT: The applicant is contractor with railways and it has been awarded a contract with KSR Bengaluru City Railway Station and service buildings at Bangalore.

The contract includes new works, repair works, addition and alteration to existing structures.

The applicant states that the Railway is considering all service buildings as business/commerce establishments and rate charged is 18 per cent (even for original works) and works related to all welfare buildings (i.e., only colonies) are charged at 12 per cent.

The applicant is seeking advance ruling as regards applicability of GST rate for works contract services doing original works with Railways.

HELD: The applicant is executing two types of works wherein, in one set of work the applicant is executing works contract for construction of new buildings and in the second set of work, it is executing works contracts not involving new construction. The correspondence of the applicant with the Railways revealed that in Zonal Works, majority of the works, it is executing are like provision of compound wall to Railway properties, laying of tiles for buildings, plumbing with new pipelines, provisions of new GLR and OHT, Staff recreation like parks, new rain water harvesting structures, painting, renovation of old structures etc. The applicant has claimed before the Railway Authorities that these are all original works as they involve new asset creation or bringing life to unused structures of Railways and these come under the works contract services as per CGST Act. [Para 9]

The issue is basically divided into two categories. One that results in the new buildings and the other repair and reconstruction of the old structures. [Para 10]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Applicant has entered into a contract for construction of a medical college with HITES which is a Government of India enterprise - Applicant has submitted that it was a sub-contractor to main contractor HITES as it is an executive agency of Central Government - Accordingly, it sought an advance ruling on question as to whether service of work contract provided by applicant as sub-contractor is taxable at rate of 12 percent for period prior to 25-1-2018 when Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 was amended by Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Whether GST rate of 12 per cent prescribed under Serial No. (ix) of Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 is effective prospectively from 25-1-2018 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, service of work contract provided by applicant as sub-contractor is not taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period before 25-1-2018 i.e. prior to issuance of amended Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 - Held, yes [Paras 25 and 26]GST : Service of work contract for construction of a medical college provided by applicant as sub-contractor to a Government enterprise is not taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period before 25-1-2018 i.e., prior to issuance of amended Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018

FACT: HITES which is a Government of India enterprise and executive agency of Ministry of Health & Welfare, Government of India, floated a tender for the construction of a medical college. Accordingly, the applicant has entered into a contract for construction of a medical college with HITES. The applicant submitted that scope of work included construction of multi storied building including water supply, sanitary and plumbing comprehensive firefighting/protection system, internal & external electrification, HVAC works, Lifts, WTP, STP, ETP, CCTV and security system, solar panel, PA system, EPABX/communication system, LAN system, site development works such as internal road & site levelling, sewer and storm water drainage work etc.

The applicant has sought an advance ruling on question as to whether the service of work contract provided by the applicant as sub-contractor is taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period prior to 25-1-2018 when Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 was amended by Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

HELD: The applicant in the present case is a sub-contractor providing services to main contractor i.e. HITES, who is an executing agency of the Ministry of Health & Welfare, Govt. of India. The work of construction of medical college has been entrusted to HITES by the Central Govt. and the applicant has provided services in the capacity of a sub-contractor. [Para 16]

To examine whether the applicant is eligible for GST at the rate of 12 per cent prior to the 25-1-2018, the main Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 vide which Central Government notified rates applicable on the services has to be referred. [Para 18]

Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 was amended by Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and new entries at Serial No. 3(iii), 3(iv), 3(v) and 3(vi) were inserted. Thereafter, again Not. No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) was amended and new entry No. (vi) was inserted vide Notification No. 24/2017-CT (Rate), dated 21-9-2017. [Para 19]

Further, the principal rate Notification No. 11/2017 was amended vide Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and inserted new entries at Serial No. 3(ix), 3(x), 3(xi) and 3(xii). The composite supply of works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor were dealt with in entries at Serial No. 3(ix) & 3(x) of the amended Notification No. 11/2017. [Para 20]

HEADNOTE: Section 97 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Advance Rulings - Application for - Whether in case of supply of services by way of construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly, except where entire consideration had been received after issuance of completion certificate by competent authority or after its first occupation, whichever was earlier, GST would be payable on two third of total amount consisting of amount charged for transfer of land or undivided share of land, and whole of consideration charged for supply of goods and service - Held, yes - Whether applicable rate of GST on said two third of total amount would be 9 per cent (CGST) and 9 per cent (SGST) - Held, yes [Para 27]CGST: In case of supply of services by way of construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly, except where entire consideration had been received after issuance of completion certificate, GST would be payable on two third of total amount consisting of amount charged for transfer of land or undivided share of land and whole of consideration charged for supply of goods and service

FACT: The assessee plans to engage itself in the development and sale of residential houses, generally floors/flats in India. The proposed modus operandi was that the assessee would either purchase land or it shall enter into collaboration agreements with various land owners whereby the assessee would acquire the right to develop the property and further sell the units developed thereon.

Post purchase of land/acquisition of land rights the applicant shall apply for the requisite approvals and then the applicant plans to get the construction work done by contractors as well as on its own.

Further, two agreements would be entered into by the assessee i.e., one for sale of undivided and impartible share in land; and another agreement for sale of superstructure.

In case where there were two transactions each represented by a separate Agreements i.e. (i.) One for sale of undivided and impartible share in land @ say Rs. 100; and (ii) another agreement for sale of superstructure @ say Rs. 15 following are the questions on which the assessee sought advance ruling on (i) Whether GST would be applicable on the sale of undivided and impartible share of land represented by Agreement to sell the land? and (ii) Whether GST would be applicable on sale of superstructure (which is under construction)? and If yes: — What will be the value on which tax is payable? and What would be the applicable rate for charging GST?

HELD: It is observed that as per section 7(2)(a), activities or transactions specified in Schedule III shall be treated neither as a supply of goods nor a supply of services. Further, paragraph 5 of the said schedule III specifically covers sale of land. Hence, sale of land is not covered under the scope of supply under GST and hence on the sale of land, no GST is payable. Similarly, sale of undivided portion of land is also outright sale of immovable property and hence outside the scope of GST. [Para 15]

However, the section 7(1)(d) read with paragraph 5(b) of schedule II specifically provides that supply of goods or supply of services include 'construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly, except where the entire consideration has been received after issuance of completion certificate, where required, by the competent authority or after its first occupation, whichever is earlier'. Hence, if construction activity is done on behalf of the buyer i.e. as a supply of goods or services to the buyer, GST is payable. [Para 16]

It is also observed that during the construction of a complex, building etc., the land and its superstructure becomes inseparable and hence, separate sale of land and its superstructure does not appear to be permissible. [Para 17]

The assessee has submitted that laws in India recognises 'land' and 'super-structure' as separate and independent immovable properties. The assessee has referred to provision of General Clauses Act, Indian Contract Act, 1872, Specific Relief Act, Transfer of Property Act, The Indian Evidence Act, Registration Act, Stamp Act, Income Tax Act etc. to claim that land and building are two different assets or immovable property and that land and superstructure can be independently sold and purchased. However, under GST, the valuation of supply of goods and services has to be done in accordance with section 15 . [Para 18]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Madhya Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Applicant-company is engaged in carrying out works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, and civil structures - A company (MPPGCL) owned by Government of Madhya Pradesh, floated a tender, for construction of some flats - Applicant raised bill for work completed at rate of 18 per cent GST to MPPGCL - However, MPPGCL is of opinion that in work under reference, applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent by treating itself as a Government entity - Whether since Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in MPPGCL and is also exercising full control over activities of said company, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for purpose of GST - Held, yes - Whether since construction activity does not have any relation to principal work of power generation entrusted by State Government to MPPGCL, works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and Notification No. 11/2017-Madhya Pradesh Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [para 5] [In favour of respondent]GST: Where activity of construction of flats allotted by MPPGCL to applicant does not have any relation to principal work of power generation entrusted by State Government to MPPCGL, work contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST)

FACT: The applicant-company (MPPGCL) is engaged in carrying out the works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, civil structures of Government, semi-Government and private undertakings.

The applicant was awarded a contract for construction of 599 flats by MPPGCL.

During the course of carrying out the construction work, the applicant company raised Running Bills (RA bills) for the portion of work completed at a point of time to MPPGCL by charging CGST and SGST at the rate of 9 per cent each, in view of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017.

MPPGCL is of the opinion that in the work under reference, the applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent (6+6), as per Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, by treating itself as a Government entity and the work allocated to the service provider is the work which is the work supplied to it by the Government.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether MPPGCL is a 'Government Entity' and whether the work contract service of construction of 599 residential quarters allotted to the applicant company, will be charged under the GST rate of 12 per cent (6+6) or 18 per cent (9+9).

HELD: In the application itself it is stated that MPPGCL has been established by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in the company and is also exercising full control over the activities of the said company. Thus, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST law, as it fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions laid down under notification No. 11/2017. [Para 5.4]

Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and inserted new entries at Serial No. 3(ix), 3(x), 3(xi) and 3(xii). The composite supply of works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor were dealt with in entries at Serial No. 3(ix) & 3(x) of the amended Notification No. 11/2017. [Para 20] The said entries at Serial No. 3(ix) and 3(x) pertained to works contract services provided by the sub-contractor to the main contractors who were in turn providing services to Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. The new entries at Serial No. 3(ix) and 3(x) inserted vide Notification dated 25-1-2018 prescribed GST rate for sub-contractor services pertaining only to the services provided by the main contractor to the Governments/Government entity which were covered in Serial No. 3(iii), Serial No. 3(vi) and Serial No. 3(vii) of the principal rate Notification No. 11/2017. [Para 21]

The entry at Serial No. 3(vi) concerned with works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor where the main contractor is providing works contract services to a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion of (a) a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession; (b) a structure meant predominantly for use as (i) an educational, (ii) a clinical, or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or (c) a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule-III to the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. [Parra 22]

Vide Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-01-2018 a new entry no. 3(ix) was inserted in the principal rate Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28-06-2017 vide which 'composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor providing services specified in item (iii) or item (vi) above to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government entity' was made taxable at the rate of 12 per cent. The said amended Notification came into effect from the date of issue of the Notification. Hence, the said Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 was issued on 25-1-2018 and in the opening paragraph of the said Notification the following is mentioned, 'In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 9, sub-section (1) of section 11, sub-section (5) of section 15 and sub-section (1) of section 16, the Central Government, on the recommendations of the Council, and on being satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest so to do, hereby makes the following further amendments in the notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated the 28-6-2017, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (i), vide number G.S.R. 690(E), dated the 28-6-2017, namely'. Accordingly, the said Notification is also published on the date of Notification in the Gazette of India. Further, an amendment in the Notification is prospective in nature, unless clearly specified to be clarificatory. Also the effective date of a Notification is always date of issue of Notification unless it is specified date of effect of the Notification. The Notification always came into effect from the date it was published in the Gazette of India and the subject Notification was issued in the Gazette of India on 25-1-2018 i.e. on the date it was issued. Therefore, Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 is applicable/came into effect prospectively and from the date of issue i.e. from 25-1-2018. [Para 23]

In view of the above it is held that the GST rate of 12 per cent prescribed under Sr. No. (ix) vide Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 is effective from the date of issue of said Notification i.e. 25-1-2018. [Para 25]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Services provided by sub-contractor to main contractor pertaining to railways - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways - It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract - Whether tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST - Held, yes [Para 11] [In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways and it executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract, tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST

FACT: The applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract.

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

1.

What tax rate to be charged by the applicant to main contractor on works contract services pertaining to railways original works contract.

2.

Whether to charge tax rate of 12 per cent GST or 18 per cent GST.

The Authority for Advance Rulings ruled that

-

The tax rate to be charged by the applicant to the main contractor would be at the rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST.

-

The tax rate to be charged would be 12 per cent.

On appeal to Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling by revenue:

HELD: There is no dispute that the services provided by the sub-contractor to its main contractor are composite supply of works contract. The main issue to decide is that the works contract services provided by the applicant are covered under item (v) of Sr. No. 3, describing the construction services, under the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 or otherwise. [Para 7]

The Authority for Advance Ruling has decided that the works contract services provided by the applicant as sub-contractor to its main contractor are squarely covered under item (v) of Sr. No. 3, describing the construction services, under the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, which provides for the concessional rate of 12 per cent GST on the composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to railways, including monorail and metro. The Authority had agreed to the applicant's contention that the works contract services provided by it or part of the works contract entered between the main contractor and railways is same, because the services performed by it as well as property in goods, i.e., material used by it in the execution of the works contract are directly getting transferred to the railways in its entirety without any change, modification or alteration therein. Thus the composite supply of any works contract undertaken by the sub-contractor as per the agreement entered between the main contractor is pertaining exclusively to railways. Therefore, by virtue of this clause 'pertaining to the railways' of item (v) of Sr. No. 3, describing the construction services, under the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, the composite supply of the sub-contractor, i.e., the applicant to its main contractor is squarely covered under this item which provides for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST to such services. [Para 8]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Haryana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of Affordable Group Housing Colony - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant is engaged in development of commercial properties - It launched an Affordable Housing Project (Affordable Group Housing Colony) in Gurugram on 1-12-2015 under scheme approved by Government of Haryana (Affordable Housing Policy, 2013) and started construction of flats over land measuring 5 acres before 31-3-2019 - Assessee further submitted an application to Directorate of Town  Country Planning, Haryana on 3-2-2018 for grant of license for setting up another Affordable Group Housing Colony over land measuring 4 acres - It started construction of flats over land measuring 4 acres after 1-4-2019 - Whether project over said land is an ongoing project as construction was started before 31-3-2019 and, therefore, rate of tax applicable in respect of flats over said land is 12 per cent (with input tax credit + land abatement) in view of Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 as applicant submitted an option to pay GST at old effective rate of 8 per cent and 12 per cent with input tax credit - Held, yes - Whether project over land measuring 4 acres is not an ongoing project as per Notification No. 3/2019 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 and applicable rate of tax on flats over said land is 0.5 per cent + 0.5 per cent (without input tax credit) - Held, yes [Paras 6.1 and 6.2] [In favour of applicant]GST : Where applicant launched an Affordable Housing Project (Affordable Group Housing Colony) in Gurugram under scheme approved by Government of Haryana (Affordable Housing Policy, 2013) and started construction of flats over land before 31-3-2019, project over said land is an ongoing project as construction was started before 31-3-2019 and, therefore, rate of tax applicable in respect of flats is 12 per cent (with input tax + land abatement) in view of Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 as applicant submitted an option to pay GST at old effective rate of 8 per cent and 12 per cent with input tax credit

FACT: The applicant is engaged in development of commercial properties.

It launched an Affordable Housing Project [Affordable Group Housing Colony] in Gurugram on 1-12-2015 under the scheme approved by the Government of Haryana [Affordable Housing Policy, 2013]. For the construction of Affordable Group Housing Colony, it was granted License No. 11 of 2014, dated 10-6-2014 by the Town & Country Planning Department, Haryana on the land measuring 5 acres located in the Revenue Estate of Village Dhankot, Sector 102, Gurugram. The building plan for construction of affordable flats was approved on 26-3-2015. The applicant started construction of flats before 31-3-2019 and the booking in respect of flats was also made in the pre-GST period.

The applicant further submitted an application to the Directorate of Town & Country Planning, Haryana on 3-2-2018 for the grant of license for setting up another Affordable Group Housing Colony over the land measuring 4 acres located in the Revenue Estate of Village Dhankot, Sector 102, Gurugram.

A separate license bearing No. 82 of 2018 for the construction of flats on the said land was granted by the Town & Country Planning Department on 6-12-2018. The building plan in respect of the said project was approved on 27-5-2019. On the basis of License No. 82 of 2018, the applicant was granted license bearing No. GGM/339/339/71/2019/33, dated 27-5-2019 by the Real Estate Regulation Authority (RERA) for construction of 595 flats in six towers.

The applicant sought advance ruling on the following question:

HEADNOTE: I. Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of residential apartment - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Whether since ongoing residential project did not fall under affordable housing scheme, services of construction of all types of residential apartments in ongoing housing project during period from 1-7-2017 to 31-3-2019 do not qualify for concessional rate of tax of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is liable to GST at rate of 18 per cent as per item (i) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 8 and 11]GST : Where ongoing residential project did not fall under affordable housing scheme, services of construction of all types of residential apartments in said ongoing housing project during period from 1-7-2017 to 31-3-2019 do not qualify for concessional rate of 12 per cent and is liable to GST at rate of 18 per cent as per item (i) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017  GST : Provisions of para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 will apply for determining taxable value of services for construction of residential flats for period from 1-7-2017 onwards where appropriation towards undivided share of land was done in pre-GST period; one-third of total amount charged for supply of services for construction of flats shall be deemed to be value of land or undivided share of land involved in said supply and applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of total amount charged for supply of services in arriving at taxable value of supply  GST : Where applicant had opted for continuation of tax payment at old rates after introduction of new tax structure for real estate sector by amendment of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, coming into effect from 1-4-2019, services of construction of residential flats in ongoing housing project are liable to GST for period from 1-4-2019 onwards at rate of 18 per cent  GST : Where booking in residential flats developed by applicant-builder are cancelled by customers, relevant date for claiming refund of taxes already paid on advances paid for booking of such flats is date of payment of tax as prescribed in Explanation 2(h) of section 54

II. Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of residential apartment - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Whether provisions of para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 will apply for determining taxable value of services for construction of residential flats for period from 1-7-2017 onwards where appropriation towards undivided share of land was done in pre-GST period - Held, yes - Whether thus, one-third of total amount charged for supply of services for construction of flats shall be deemed to be value of land or undivided share of land involved in said supply and applicant is eligible to avail deduction of one-third of total amount charged for supply of services in arriving at taxable value of supply - Held, yes [Paras 9 and 11]

III. Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of residential apartments - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant - builder was engaged in service of construction of residential apartments in ongoing housing project - A new tax structure for real estate sector was introduced with effect from 1-4-2019 onwards by amendment of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 vide Notification No. 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 which provided provision for continuing old tax rate as it existed up to 31-3-2019 for ongoing housing projects - Applicant had opted for continuation of tax payment at old rates - Whether thus, services of construction of residential flats in ongoing housing project are liable to GST for period from 1-4-2019 onwards at rate of 18 per cent as per Sl No. 3(if) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 10 and 11]

headnotes.text: Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of residential colony - Heading 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant is engaged in construction of residential and commercial complexes - It has been awarded a contract by Airport Authority of India for construction of residential colony staff and employees - Whether construction of residential colony by applicant attracts GST at rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) as per entry at SI. No. 3(vi)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 10]GST : Where applicant has been awarded a contract by Airport Authority of India for construction of residential colony for staff and employees, construction of residential colony by applicant attracts GST at rate of 12 per cent as per entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Construction Service - Staff quarters of government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Whether supply of service of construction of staff quarters to be provided to government entity Uttar Pradesh Rajkiya Nirman Nigam Ltd., (UPRNN) is eligible for concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent in terms of S. No. 3 (vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Applicant is required to construct staff quarters for Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) under work order - HELD : Composite supply of works contract by way of construction of residential quarters meant for use of employees of ESIC can be considered as construction of civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry or any other business or profession - UPRNN is a government entity - Such service is eligible for concessional rate when it is provided to Union territory or local authority and is not eligible for concessional rate if provided to government authority or government entity as per amendment made by Notification No. 15/2021-Central Tax (Rate) - Services to be provided by applicant are not covered under Sl. No. 3 (vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 to avail 12 per cent GST rate and same will be covered under residuary clause (xii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 attracting 18 per cent GST [Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5.2, 5.3.2 and 5.4.2] [In favour of revenue]GST : Supply of service of construction of staff quarters to be provided to a government entity is not entitled to concessional rate of 12% GST; such service attracts 18% GST

Residential quarters construction - Construction Service - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional Rate - Appellant-assessee is engaged in civil execution contracts - It is awarded with a project by government entity NPCIL for carrying construction of quarters for residential usage of their employees engaged in nuclear power project - AAR ruled that execution of works contract service for construction of residential quarters for employees is not covered under Serial No. 3(vi) of Notification 11/2017-CT-Rate, dated 28-6-2017 and applicable rate of GST is 18 per cent as per Serial No. 3(xii) of Notification 11/2017-CT-Rate, dated 28-6-2017 - HELD: From a joint reading of MOA of NPCIL and relevant certificate, it is evident that works relating to construction of residential quarters are objectives incidental or ancillary to attainment of main object of NPCIL which is a government entity - However, vide amendment made to entry 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T.(Rate), dated 28-6-2017 vide Notification No. 15/2021-C.T.(Rate), dated 18-11-2021 effective from 1-1-2022, term 'Government entity' stands omitted in class of recipients from 1-1-2022 - Therefore, appellant-assessee is eligible for concessional rate of tax at 12 per cent as per entry 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) read with corresponding Notification Under TNGSTA for period up to 31-12-2021 and GST is applicable at 18 per cent from 31-12-2021 as per aforesaid amendment [Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8.1 - 10] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Where execution of works contract service for construction of residential quarters by applicant-civil contractor is exclusively meant for use of employees of government entity NPCIL, and aforesaid construction is ancillary to attainment of main object of NPCIL, applicant is eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST for period up to 31-12-2021

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of civil structures - Heading No. 9954 (Construction Services) - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works Contract - Applicant has been awarded a project by Airport Authority of India (AAI) which is in nature of works contract - Scope of project is development and upgradation of Airports by construction or extension of Runway, construction of new Taxi track, Apron, Isolation bay, Perimeter road and other allied works - It has sought advance ruling in respect of applicable rate of tax on works allotted by AAI - It is found that applicant is undertaking a works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for AAI which are used in process of commerce and business - Entry at Serial number 3(vi)(a) specifically provides that works be 'meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession - Whether therefore, works contract performed by applicant cannot be considered as covered under Serial No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 6 per cent, but are more appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax, dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent - Held, yes [Paras 7 and 8]GST : Works contract of construction of a civil structure or any other original works for Airport Authorities of India performed by applicant being used in process of commerce and business is appropriately covered under Serial No.3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, liable to tax at 9 per cent

Housing construction - Construction service - Works contract service for State Housing Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction services are provided to Karnataka Housing Board with respect to construction of Police Station as a main contractor/sub-contractor - Karnataka Housing Board having been established under Karnataka Housing Board Act, 1962 and carrying out functions entrusted by State Government is to be considered as Government Entity as defined under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 and liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 13, 14 and 16 to 18]

Residential quarters construction - Construction Service - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional Rate - Appellant-assessee is engaged in civil execution contracts - It is awarded with a project by government entity NPCIL for carrying construction of quarters for residential usage of their employees engaged in nuclear power project - AAR ruled that execution of works contract service for construction of residential quarters for employees is not covered under Serial No. 3(vi) of Notification 11/2017-CT-Rate, dated 28-6-2017 and applicable rate of GST is 18 per cent as per Serial No. 3(xii) of Notification 11/2017-CT-Rate, dated 28-6-2017 - HELD: From a joint reading of MOA of NPCIL and relevant certificate, it is evident that works relating to construction of residential quarters are objectives incidental or ancillary to attainment of main object of NPCIL which is a government entity - However, vide amendment made to entry 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T.(Rate), dated 28-6-2017 vide Notification No. 15/2021-C.T.(Rate), dated 18-11-2021 effective from 1-1-2022, term 'Government entity' stands omitted in class of recipients from 1-1-2022 - Therefore, appellant-assessee is eligible for concessional rate of tax at 12 per cent as per entry 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) read with corresponding Notification Under TNGSTA for period up to 31-12-2021 and GST is applicable at 18 per cent from 31-12-2021 as per aforesaid amendment [Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8.1 - 10] [Partly in favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications : Entry 3(vi) and Serial No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 15/2021-C.T (Rate), dated 18-11-2021 effective from 1-1-2022

II. Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant entered into a contract with developer for construction of residential apartment - Applicant has not provided any evidence to effect that above project is covered under affordable housing project in terms of Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Whether if projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, contract of supply by applicant would be covered under Entry No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and at 6 per cent SGST and, otherwise said services will be liable to tax at rate of 9 per cent under CGST Act and at rate of 9 per cent under KGST Act as provided in Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 14]

I. Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant entered into a contract with developer for construction of residential apartment - Whether since contract is for construction of an immovable property, same is covered under works contract as per section 2(119) - Held, yes [Para 12]GST : If projects are affordable housing projects and are given infrastructure status as per notification of Government of India, construction service provided by applicant to developer under residential project is liable to tax at rate of 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent KGST as provided in Sl. No. 3(v)(da) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; else, services will be liable to tax at rate of 9 per cent under CGST Act and at rate of 9 per cent under KGST Act as provided in Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017  GST : Where applicant, engaged in business of civil works contract entered into an agreement with developer for construction of residential apartment project, since contract is for construction of an immovable property, same is covered under works contract as per section 2(119)

Contruction of medical institute - Construction service - Composite supply of works contract service to Government entity - Heading No 9954 - Concessional rate - Post Graduate Medical Institute and super specialty hospital are constructed for SAIL through sub-contractor under Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) contract on turnkey basis - Aforesaid contract being for design, engineering, procurement and construction of medical institute and hospital, is an immovable property and involves supply of all goods and services required for its completion; it is to be considered as Works Contract under section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - SAIL being a Government Entity and construction of said medical institute and hospital being a clinical establishment for medical care without any profit motive and not used for commerce, industry or any other business or profession, work is liable to 12 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) or 3(vi)(b) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended - When a sub-contractor is allowed to discharge GST at a concessional rate for supplies made to principal contractor who in turn makes such supplies to Government Entity SAIL, different rate of GST is not permissible for such supplies made by principal contractor [Section 2(30) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Odisha Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6.2 to 7.0] [In favour of assessee]GST : Construction of Medical Institute and super specialty hospital for SAIL through sub-contractor under EPC contract on turnkey basis is liable to 12 per cent GST   GST : Application seeking Advance Ruling on question as to whether tax paid over and above tax liability can be regarded as tax-in-excess to claim refund thereof, does not fall for consideration under section 97(2) of CGST Act, 2017

Classification of services - Construction services (NR) - Applicant, a partnership firm of builders and developers is to undertake an affordable housing project on their land - It seeks advance ruling on what is rate of tax to be levied on sale of flats/units to prospective buyers - According to sub-item (da) of item (v) of Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate) 25-1-2018, low-cost houses up to a carpet area of 60 square metres per house is an affordable housing project which has been given infrastructure status vide notification of Government of India - Whether since project undertaken by applicant falls under definition of 'Affordable Housing project' concessional rate of taxes to be levied is 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) - Held, yes [Para 5]GST: Rate of tax to be levied is 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land) in case of Affordable Housing Project  GST : Where concessional rate of tax of 12 per cent on affordable housing project is levied by GST Council, builder or developer having paid GST of 18 per cent or 28 per cent on inputs and capital goods used in construction of flats, will not be required to pay GST on construction service of flats, etc., as they would have enough ITC (input tax credits) in their books to pay output GST

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - State Police Housing and Infrastructure Corporation is a company of Government of Karnataka State incorporated under companies Act, 1956 and all shares are held by Government of Karnataka; hence, it qualifies to be considered as a government entity-Works contract services executed for construction of high security prison are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.1 and 14] [In favour of revenue]GST : Works contract awarded by State Police Housing and Infrastructure Corporation for construction of High Security Prison is liable to 18 per cent GST  GST : Works contract awarded by area Development Board for construction of International Center and Museum is liable to 18 per cent GST  GST : Works contract awarded by Residential Educational Institutions Society for construction of residential school complex is liable to 18 per cent GST  GST : Where contract was awarded to applicant by public works department of State Government for construction of Airport Terminal Building, allied buildings/facilities and associated works and development of airport, it is liable to 18 per cent GST
